matches.rationale: Finding 1 identifies the exact same formula (ρ definition and S̃ = S·√ρ(v_j)) and the same logical contradiction: high-density regions get increased rather than decreased similarity, contradicting the stated bias-mitigation goal.

No finding addresses the claimed contradiction about boundary features being labeled 'informative'/weighted equally versus the SVDD notion of noisy boundary points; finding 2 instead critiques an unrelated aspect of the hypersphere equation (inner product vs squared-norm constraint), a different locus and mechanism.

pred_verdicts.rationale: Correctly identifies the same mathematical inconsistency in the density compensation correction term as GT1.

Raises a distinct, plausible issue about the hypersphere containment formula's use of inner product vs squared distance, which is not the ground-truth defect about noisy vs informative boundary features.
Flags a separate, specific concern about taking log of an unnormalized similarity score in Eq. (7), unrelated to either ground-truth defect.
